abstract: Transforming growth factors are known to induce anchorage-independent growth of non-transformed cells, and are released by a variety of cells, including MSV-transformed cells. This study demonstrates that the differentiated cells derived from F9 and PC-13 embryonal carcinoma cells, but not the parental cells themselves, respond by increased growth to several factors released by MSV-transformed cells, including partially purified sarcoma growth factor. The chemical properties of the growth-promoting activity are shown to match the chemical properties of the transforming growth factors released by MSV-transformed cells. Furthermore, F9 and PC-13 embryonal carcinoma cells, which do not respond to factors released by MSV-transformed cells, are shown to release factors with transforming growth factor activity. Based on the close relationship between mouse embryonal carcinoma cells and cells of early mouse embryos, it is suggested that molecules with transforming growth factor activity may play a role during the early stages of mammalian development.
abstract_ja: 形質転換増殖因子は、非形質転換細胞の足場非依存性増殖を誘導することが知られており、多様な細胞から放出される。本研究では、F9およびPC-13胎児性癌細胞から分化した細胞は、親細胞とは異なり、MSV形質転換細胞から放出された複数の因子(部分精製された肉腫増殖因子を含む)に応答して増殖が増加することを示した。増殖促進活性の化学的性質は、MSV形質転換細胞から放出される形質転換増殖因子のものと一致した。さらに、MSV因子に応答しないF9およびPC-13胎児性癌細胞も、形質転換増殖因子活性を持つ因子を放出していた。マウス胎児性癌細胞と初期マウス胚細胞との密接な関係に基づき、形質転換増殖因子活性を持つ分子は哺乳類の初期発生の段階で役割を果たす可能性があると考えられる。
